candidates.background: Fourth-generation East Austinite who has worked in healthcare since 2007; opposed the 2025 Prop Q tax increase and the HOME code changes.

own_words.text: My support for growth has one condition: it must be smart in scale, fit neighborhood character, and include real anti-displacement protections.
Supports Prop I: "In most businesses, standard practice is to have an outside audit."
Does not support smaller minimum lot sizes; thinks voters should get another say on Project Connect.

candidates.name: Alexandria Anderson
candidates.background: Personal training business owner and former professional track athlete; chair of the MLK Neighborhood Association and two city commissions.

own_words.text: We must build infrastructure alongside growth, not after it.
Supports Prop I "with guardrails." On Project Connect: "Yes, because it's a step," but says it does not reach far East Austin.
Does not support more data centers until noise, water and energy protections are in place.

candidates.name: Amber K. Goodwin
candidates.background: Travis County assistant district attorney 2022 to 2026; chaired the city's gun violence task force; worked for Giffords and co-founded the Community Violence Legal Network.

own_words.text: I will invest in community-led public health approaches to tackle safety including prevention, housing stability, and mental health services.
Opposes Prop I. Supports Project Connect. Says ICE "should be abolished but also prosecuted."
Proposes a "D1 Economic Opportunity Fund" to pair growth with transit and small-business loans.

candidates.name: Michael Nahas
candidates.background: Computer scientist and economist; chaired Austin's Economic Prosperity Commission and served on the board of the urbanist group AURA.

own_words.text: I found Austin's pension borrowing is wasting 1/3 of our property tax on interest.
To lower the rent, just allow more housing and more locations. It's a supply and demand issue.
Supports Prop I with a concern about its tax-election timing; would reject Project Connect if proposed new today.

candidates.background: Third-generation East Austinite pursuing associate degrees; has worked at Texas REALTORS, the appraisal district and Austin 311. LWV lists only an Eventbrite donation page.

own_words.text: I don't consider myself a politician. I consider myself a neighbor.
Supports Prop I; would keep large data centers out of residential and inner-city areas.
Has "a little gray area of concern" on Project Connect but would not rule out supporting it.

candidates.name: Misael Ramos
candidates.background: Business analyst and community organizer; former board president of Blackland Community Development Corporation; ran for this seat in 2022. Endorsed by DSA. Faces a misdemeanor riot charge from an ICE protest, which he disputes.

own_words.text: We have taken a pledge to not take corporate or real estate interests.
Be intentional about building deeply affordable housing, and make it cheaper for affordable housing developers.
Calls for ICE abolition and a moratorium on data centers; supports Project Connect but wants D1 included.

Wants Project Connect completed and light rail expanded west.

candidates.name: Neha Shah
candidates.background: Tech entrepreneur and immigrant with 20 years in tech, startups and nonprofits; a volunteer deputy voter registrar. Says the Dog's Head vote pushed her to run.

own_words.text: Public safety means community investment, not just bigger police budgets.

I'm pro-innovation, but not anti-regulation.

scope_plain: Voters in Texas House District 73: Comal County and western Hays County, including Wimberley, Woodcreek and Dripping Springs. The City of San Marcos is not in it; it is listed for rural Hays addresses outside the city.
office_explainer: One of 150 state representatives: writes and votes on Texas laws and the state budget.
why_it_matters: The Republican incumbent, in office since 2023, against a Democratic retired school principal. Water, growth and school vouchers are the main issues in the candidates’ own materials.

candidates.name: Carrie Isaac
candidates.background: State representative since January 2023. Nonprofit executive, including executive director of DEWIT, which gives financial help to veterans. Stephen F. Austin State University. Lives in Hays County.

own_words.text: Cut property taxes, starting by eliminating school maintenance and operations property taxes (2022 survey).
Secure the border by 'building a wall and stopping magnet policies that encourage illegal immigration' (2022 survey).
Lists property tax reform and 'education freedom' as the policy areas she cares most about (2022 survey).

candidates.name: Merrie Fox
candidates.background: Retired public school teacher and principal (31 years) with a PhD in educational leadership; now a nonprofit executive director. Says she has lived in the district for 45 years.

own_words.text: 'If elected, I will work to eliminate vouchers' and state-sponsored religious instruction in schools.
Standardize groundwater districts' authority statewide 'to help prevent over-pumping by commercial wells.'
Give county officials power to manage growth, 'especially regarding hyperscale data centers.'
